guide.title: Beethoven, String Quartet No. 16, Op. 135 – III. Lento assai, cantante e tranquillo
guide.overview: This is a slow, quiet movement in three sections. It is in 6/8 time and its home key is Db major. The keys and chords here are estimated by computer, so some labels may be imprecise. The first violin usually carries the tune, but the analysis often rates this as uncertain. Listen for the hushed middle section and the calm return of the opening mood.

listening_points.headline: A soft opening and the first tune
listening_points.text: The movement begins softly [m. 1]. The second violin probably leads the first bar. Then Violin 1 takes the tune [m. 2-4], while the others accompany. The key is Db major.

listening_points.headline: The tune is shared among the voices
listening_points.text: Violin 1 keeps the tune at first [m. 5-6]. After that the lead is unclear. Violin 1 and the viola probably share it [m. 7]. In [m. 9] the parts move as independent lines. A crescendo (gradual swell) is marked.

listening_points.headline: Swelling and fading, still in Db major
listening_points.text: The music swells and fades in small waves [m. 11-12]. In [m. 12] the parts move together in chords, which is called homophonic texture. Violin 1 probably leads through [m. 13-15]. A crescendo is marked in [m. 15].

listening_points.headline: A new key and sudden accents
listening_points.text: The estimated key moves to Ab major [m. 16]. This is a modulation, a change of key. The marking rfz is a sudden strong accent, and it appears in [m. 17-19]. The parts mostly move in chords.

listening_points.headline: Closing the first part
listening_points.text: Violin 1 probably leads again in [m. 20-21]. The lines become more independent [m. 21-22]. Swelling and fading are both marked here. The estimated key stays Ab major.

listening_points.headline: Slower and hushed: the middle section
listening_points.text: The tempo marking changes to Più lento, which means slower [m. 23]. The dynamic drops to pp, very soft. The parts move in chords. Violin 1 leads. The estimated key turns to G# minor [m. 24-27], which is darker.

listening_points.headline: Deeper into minor, with a rise in volume
listening_points.text: The estimated key shifts to C# minor [m. 28]. The level rises from pp to p by [m. 29]. An rfz accent is marked there. Violin 1 leads, with less certainty near the end. The chords still move together.

listening_points.headline: Back to Db major and the original tempo
listening_points.text: Db major returns [m. 32]. The viola probably leads there, with the others accompanying. Section 3 begins at the original tempo [m. 33]. Violin 1 probably takes the tune again [m. 33-34].

listening_points.headline: A brief visit to F minor
listening_points.text: The estimated key darkens to F minor [m. 35-39]. The four parts mostly move as independent lines. The lead is unclear; Violin 1 and the viola probably share it. The music is soft throughout.

listening_points.headline: Home key again, with interwoven lines
listening_points.text: Db major returns [m. 40]. The voices weave their own lines, and this continues through [m. 44]. Swelling and fading are marked in [m. 41-42]. Violin 1 probably leads in [m. 41-45].

listening_points.headline: Toward the computer-estimated peak
listening_points.text: The lines stay independent [m. 46-52]. A crescendo is marked in [m. 48], and a diminuendo, a gradual softening, in [m. 49]. A sudden accent rfz comes in [m. 51]. A computer estimate marks [m. 52] as the loudest or busiest point. It is still marked p.

listening_points.headline: A very soft close
listening_points.text: The music settles to pp, very soft [m. 53]. Violin 1 leads over a quiet accompaniment. The movement ends in Db major.

glossary.explanation: A change from one key to another. It can brighten or darken the mood.
The parts move together in chords, with one main line on top.
Each instrument plays its own line, and the lines weave together.
A sudden, strong accent on a note or chord.

review.note: prose corrected after a line-by-line review against the facts
